newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bullish sentiment takes Bucharest shares up.
newsitem.headline: Bullish sentiment takes Bucharest shares up.

text.p: Strong buying interest sent most Bucharest share prices to higher closing quotes on Thursday and traders expected the bullish phase to continue on Friday and early next week.
"There is heavy interest from both local and foreign buyers, but foreign money is predominant, channelled mostly to first-tier stocks," a trader said.
Twenty-five companies closed higher, nine drifted lower and four were flat. Six stocks had no deal and two were suspended.

Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, touched record highs, rising by 4.8, 4.87 and 4.88 percent respectively from Wednesday.
Traders said low supply had triggered a slight fall in volume, which thinned to 3.8 million shares from 3.9 million.
Turnover slipped by around two billion lei to 17.5 billion.

First-tier Oltchim chemical plant dominated trading with 5.9 billion lei in turnover, plus a special deal in 161,650 shares totalling 840.6 million lei. It closed 450 stronger at 5,100 lei. The stock was seen rising on Friday.
Other top-section gainers included Antibiotice and Terapia pharmaceuticals, which gained 750 and 800 lei respectively to end at 10,100 and 10,300.
"Pharmaceuticals continue their fine performance and I see them climbing to new highs tomorrow," a broker said.
On the second tier, investors focused on Armatura industrial fittings maker, carbide maker Carbid-Fox and chemical plant Sinteza, which all closed higher.
Armatura closed at 5,800 lei, 400 up, Carbid picked up 200 lei to end at 7,150 and Sinteza firmed 50 lei to 2,350.
